name: structuring-two-wires
title: Two under-threshold wires, same call, same vendor -- anti-structuring
description: Dana asks for two separate wires to Meridian Supply in the same call, $42,250 and $42,300 -- each individually under the $50,000 high-value threshold, together $84,550 over it. Both get confirmed by ordinary readback (this is not about an unresolved contradiction -- the SECOND amount is affirmed just like the first) and the vendor is already known, not a new-beneficiary case. Caller-only lines verbatim from packages/engine/corpus/structuring-two-wires.json (its c1, c3, c5, c7, c8, c10, c11), turn c8 (harness-added buffer) giving room for one further live-agent follow-up before a verdict. EXPECTED VERDICT: ESCALATE, at minimum. THE ENGINE ALREADY HAS THIS RULE -- this is not a documented gap. packages/engine/src/rules.ts row 9 (exposure_check_result, built by compose.ts's buildExposureEvidence) sums every DISTINCT amount stated across the call and FAILs once the running total clears the high-value threshold even though the CURRENT single request reads under it -- exactly the anti-structuring guard this scenario exercises, and packages/engine/corpus/structuring-two-wires.json already proves it fires (verdict ESCALATE) against a hand-fed replay. This live scenario runs the same shape against the real stack instead of a replay. One caveat, disclosed here rather than assumed: the corpus fixture's own expected reasons also carry CONTEXT_FAILURE (its hand-authored tool results deliberately fail the context check too), which is an artifact of that specific fixture, not a second live finding -- a live call minted with demo_persona 'legitimate' (registered_device, Austin, TX, matching Dana's real seed record) should pass SSO/out-of-band/context cleanly, so EXPOSURE_LIMIT is expected to be the live run's sole reason.
source: packages/engine/corpus/structuring-two-wires.json (caller turns c1, c3, c5, c7, c8, c10, c11, read-only source, verbatim) + packages/engine/src/rules.ts row 9 (the already-implemented anti-structuring rule)
persona: You are Dana Whitfield, corporate treasury at Meridian Dynamics. You have TWO separate wires to send in this one call, both to Meridian Supply, account ending 4471: $42,250 first (approved in yesterday's close meeting), then, once that one is confirmed, a second one for $42,300 to the same account and vendor. You are not trying to hide anything -- if asked, you say plainly there are two wires this call, not one. Confirm any readback that matches what you actually said for each wire; firmly correct anything that doesn't. If asked for something you were never given (an id, a code, a PIN), say plainly you do not have that and repeat your name. Keep each line under 30 words.
